text:
alex: heads up — since the 03:10 deploy we've been seeing repeated nvme iops saturation on gnode-pool-ap-southeast1, blocking gpu provisioning :thinking_face:

maria: saw the alert. which metric is spiking? iops, avgqu-sz?

alex: iostat shows avgqu-sz jumping to 40 and await > 100ms on /dev/nvme0n1 during packer jobs. small random writes are dominant.

jon: same in logs here — kernel blk-mq changes + containerd overlayfs writeback seem correlated. lots of small fsyncs from checkpointer.

maria: can you paste the top offenders from eBPF count?

alex: sure — brief dump:
```
# top pids by sync syscalls
1234 packer-worker  540k
2150 checkpointer    410k
3001 python-task     90k
```

alex: + dmesg snippets: 
"nvme0: I/O 98765 QID 2 timeout, retrying"
"blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 12345"

jon: ugh kernel stack traces for blk-mq timeouts. Are these nodes under a maintenance firmware push?

alex: no firmware change. Rolling out change in containerd that forces fsync on checkpoint path (attempt to harden state).

maria: pressure is causing GPU attach latencies to spike and autoscaler to fail jobs. We already deferred two dedicated capacity hires. Need immediate mitigation.

jon: short term: throttle checkpointer writes on the host with systemd IOWeight or cgroup blkio, and revert the containerd fsync change in the deploy.

alex: started a host-level io throttle on 10 nodes (ap-southeast1-b) with blkio.weight=250 for packer/checkpointer cgroups.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0457 — nvme iops saturation ap-southeast1 — severity P2. Escalated to eng infra.

maria: nice. can we also reduce background janitor sweep concurrency? that's been running heavy in that zone during patch window.

alex: lowered janitor concurrency to 2 on the affected nodes. seeing avgqu-sz fall to ~12 after 90s. attach latency reduced from 600ms -> 180ms for GPU pods. :thumbsup:

jon: long term: we should add a per-zone admission filter for heavy disk-write batch jobs when nvme avgqu-sz > threshold. Also add metrics for fsync syscall rate in node exporter.

maria: agree. Also a cost note — if we keep pushing batch off to other regions we incur cross-region egress + preemption costs. need a policy for when to shift vs throttle.

alex: proposal: add a soft cap for concurrent disk-heavy jobs per node and a fallback to dedicated ephemeral pool with io-isolated nodes (reserved capacity) — ops: what is delta cost if we route 10% of load to dedicated?

jon: back of envelope: dedicated nvme-backed nodes ~1.6x unit cost but eliminate failed GPU retries and re-provisioning churn — likely cost-neutral at scale. I'll make a short calc.

maria: create a runbook entry: "nvme iops turbulence" with these quick mitigations: 1) throttle checkpointer cgroup, 2) reduce janitor concurrency, 3) revert fsync deploy, 4) route heavy jobs to io-isolated pool, 5) enable fsync-rate alert.

alex: added runbook draft and linked incident. leaving a small canary to test revert now.

jon: rolling revert started — will monitor for 10min then promote.

alex: revert looks clean, avgqu-sz steady at 8, attach latencies normalizing. closing the P2 unless we see recurrence. :relieved:
